title: Car Chasing
description: Car chase cinematography covers pursuit from a second vehicle, matching speed, the road as the set. Two machines stay in a line of action; this is the hunter's lens, not a locked interior.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Two machines, one argument. The camera is in the chasing car, or in a picture car matching the pair.
Trees, lamps, and lane lines shear because both vehicles are moving. A parked conversation does not need it.
Two cars in a lot is not a chase. Do not cut to a drone unless you mean aerial; the grammar here is matching speed from another machine.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Process trailer, chase vehicle, or a matched virtual path. Long lens compresses the gap; wide includes both machines and the road.
Keep a line of action. Prompt: Car-chase coverage of [Subject], pursuit from a second vehicle, matching speed, road as the set.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a beauty pass of one car. The tell: no second machine, no smear, no line of action.
The fix: pursuit from another vehicle, matching speed, something in the world streaking.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Car Chasing in film?
Car chasing is coverage of pursuit from a second vehicle at matching speed, with the road as the set and two machines in one argument.
Car Chasing vs Buckle Up
Buckle up is locked inside one cabin. Car chasing is the hunter's lens from another vehicle, keeping a pursuit relationship.
When should I use Car Chasing?
Use it when two machines are in pursuit. Do not use it for a parked talk or a single-car product pass.
How do I prompt Car Chasing for AI image or video?
Write pursuit from a second vehicle and matching speed. Example: Car-chase coverage of [Subject], pursuit from a second vehicle, matching speed, road as the set.
